record.original_question: Using the same definition of P* for orthogonal projections from a point P to the sides of a triangle ABC, find proofs of the Gergonne-point and Nagel-point existence criteria that avoid reliance on Maple or computational algebra and are more geometric or elegant.

evidence.quote: would be interesting to come up with proofs that are more elegant, more geometric, and less computational.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let ABC be a triangle in the Euclidean plane, and for any point P in the plane let P* denote the triangle whose vertices are the orthogonal projections of P onto the three (extended) sides BC, CA, AB of ABC (the pedal triangle of P with respect to ABC).

Consider the following two known concurrence criteria, each of which gives a characterization of a special point of the triangle in terms of pedal-triangle constructions of the type P → P*:

(i) (Gergonne-point criterion) A characterization of the Gergonne point of ABC — the point at which the three cevians joining each vertex of ABC to the point where the incircle touches the opposite side concur — expressed via the operation P ↦ P*.

(ii) (Nagel-point criterion) A characterization of the Nagel point of ABC — the point at which the three cevians joining each vertex of ABC to the point where the opposite side is touched by the corresponding excircle concur — expressed via the same operation P ↦ P*.

Provide proofs of these two concurrence criteria that are purely synthetic / geometric in nature, avoiding any reliance on computer algebra systems or extensive symbolic computation. The goal is to obtain proofs whose steps consist of classical Euclidean-geometric arguments (for example using Ceva's theorem, isogonal/isotomic conjugacy, projective duality, properties of pedal triangles, Desargues' or Brianchon's theorem, trigonometric identities, etc.) rather than coordinate or algebraic verification.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search reveals substantial literature on the Gergonne and Nagel points, including synthetic treatments via Ceva's theorem, isotomic conjugacy, Brianchon's theorem, and generalizations to simplices. However, no specific source was located that gives elegant non-computational proofs of the particular pedal-triangle ("P*") concurrence criteria asked here. The status of this specific request is therefore unclear from available sources.

status_evidence.title: Generalized Gergonne and Nagel Points (Odehnal)
status_evidence.snippet: Synthetic treatment generalizing Gergonne and Nagel points using perspectivity and classical incidence theorems.
status_evidence.claim: Synthetic / geometric methods exist for related Gergonne/Nagel concurrence statements, but not specifically for the P*-criterion phrased here.

status_evidence.title: A note on the Nagel and Gergonne points
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses concurrence properties and isotomic relationship between Gergonne and Nagel points.
status_evidence.claim: Standard concurrence proofs use Ceva and isotomic conjugacy; the specific pedal-projection variant remains without a published elegant proof to our knowledge.
